content: These references are formatted in a way that includes the authors, titles, publication sources, years, volumes, and page numbers. They cover a wide range of topics, including parasitic diseases, zoonotic infections, public health issues, and epidemiological studies. 1. A study conducted in the Philippines utilized real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to assess ion presence in water buffaloes. This research was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2010 (Volume 82, Issue 4, Pages 646-652). 2. Sinuon M and colleagues reported on the outcomes of an eight-year control program targeting Schistosoma mekongi in two endemic provinces of Cambodia. Their findings were published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2007 (Volume 101, Issue 1, Pages 34-39). 3. Wu WH and collaborators described the strategies and processes involved in eliminating schistosomiasis in several Chinese provinces, including Guangdong, Shanghai, Fujian, Guangxi, and Zhejiang. This work was included in a book edited by Wang LD, titled The Course and Perspectives in Schistosomiasis Control in China, published by People's Health Press in Beijing in 2006 (Page 401). 4. Leonardo LR and colleagues discussed the challenges and strategies for controlling schistosomiasis in the Philippines. Their work appeared in Acta Tropica in 2002 (Volume 82, Issue 2, Pages 295-299). 5. Tallo VL and co-authors questioned whether mass treatment is the optimal strategy for schistosomiasis elimination. Their analysis was published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2008 (Volume 86, Issue 10, Pages 765-771). 6. Wang LD and colleagues proposed a strategy to control the transmission of Schistosoma japonicum in China. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2009 (Volume 360, Issue 2, Pages 121-128). 7. Utzinger J and collaborators reviewed the progress made in combating schistosomiasis in China, referring to it as a long march. This review was published in Acta Tropica in 2005 (Volume 96, Issues 2-3, Pages 69-96). 8. McManus DP and Loukas A provided an update on the current status of vaccines for schistosomiasis. Their review was published in Clinical Microbiology Reviews in 2008 (Volume 21, Issue 1, Pages 225-242). 9. Zhu HM and colleagues examined the impact of the Three Gorges Dam on the potential transmission of schistosomiasis in regions along the Yangtze River. Their findings were published in EcoHealth in 2008 (Volume 5, Issue 2, Pages 137-148). 10. Croce D and collaborators evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a successful schistosomiasis control program implemented in Cambodia between 1995 and 2006. Their analysis was published in Acta Tropica in 2010 (Volume 113, Issue 3, Pages 279-284). 11. Keiser J and Utzinger J reviewed foodborne trematodiases, highlighting their clinical and epidemiological aspects. This review was published in Clinical Microbiology Reviews in 2009 (Volume 22, Issue 3, Pages 466-483). 12. Sripa B and colleagues demonstrated the role of liver fluke infections in inducing cholangiocarcinoma. Their study was published in PLoS Medicine in 2007 (Volume 4, Issue 7, Article 201). 13. Sripa B provided an updated overview of the pathobiology of opisthorchiasis. This review was published in Acta Tropica in 2003 (Volume 88, Issue 3, Pages 209-220). 14. Mas-Coma S, Bargues MD, and Valero MA reviewed fascioliasis and other plant-borne trematode zoonoses. Their work appeared in the International Journal of Parasitology in 2005 (Volume 35, Issues 11-12, Pages 1255-1278). 15. Phan VT and colleagues identified farm-level risk factors for fishborne zoonotic trematode infections in small-scale fish farms in northern Vietnam. Their findings were published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2010 (Volume 4, Issue 7, Article 742). 16. A joint WHO/FAO workshop held in Hanoi, Vietnam, in November 2002, addressed foodborne trematode infections in Asia. The report was published by the World Health Organization in 2004. 17. Keiser J and Utzinger J discussed emerging foodborne trematodiases in a review published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2005 (Volume 11, Issue 10, Pages 1507-1514). 18. The WHO Technical Report Series No. 971 (2012) outlined research priorities for zoonoses and marginalized infections, as reported by the TDR Disease Reference Group. 19. Remington JS and colleagues provided a comprehensive overview of toxoplasmosis in their book Infectious Diseases of the Fetus and Newborn Infant, 6th edition, published by Elsevier Saunders in 2006 (Pages 947-1091). 20. Rosso F and collaborators presented progress in science and action at the International Conference on Women and Infectious Diseases held in Atlanta, Georgia, in 2006. 21. The CDC assessed the efficacy of chemotherapy for cryptosporidiosis in males with AIDS, as reported in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 1982 (Volume 31, Issue 44, Pages 589-592). 22. Xiao L and Fayer R conducted molecular characterization of Cryptosporidium and Giardia species and genotypes, focusing on zoonotic transmission. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Parasitology in 2008 (Volume 38, Issue 11, Pages 1239-1255). 23. McLaughlin J and colleagues performed a molecular epidemiological analysis of Cryptosporidium spp. in the UK, genotyping 1,705 human fecal samples and 105 livestock samples. Their study was published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2000 (Volume 38, Issue 11, Pages 3984-3990). 24. Feltus DC and collaborators provided evidence supporting zoonotic transmission of Cryptosporidium spp. in Wisconsin. Their findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2006 (Volume 44, Issue 12, Pages 4303-4308). 25. Smith KE and colleagues reported outbreaks of enteric infections caused by multiple pathogens associated with calves at a farm day camp. Their study was published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 2004 (Volume 23, Issue 12, Pages 1098-1104).
